The technology is not the bottleneck. Your organization is.

Oxford Economics research published this month confirms what high-performing executive teams already suspect: the biggest obstacle to enterprise AI is not model capability. It is business readiness — data quality, process maturity, and governance infrastructure.

Fast-growth companies have the largest AI opportunity, yet few are capturing it. The gap is not access to models. Every company on earth can call GPT-6.1 or Claude today. The gap is whether your data is clean enough, your processes are documented enough, and your governance is rigorous enough to trust AI with mission-critical decisions.

This finding reframes the entire AI investment conversation. Boards asking "which AI model should we use?" are asking the wrong question. The right question is: "Are our data pipelines, process definitions, and compliance frameworks ready to support autonomous execution?"

The implication for 2027 planning: AI budgets should be weighted toward data infrastructure, process reengineering, and governance frameworks — not model licensing. The model is a commodity. Readiness is the competitive moat.

Organizations that treat AI deployment as a technology procurement exercise will continue to stall. Those that treat it as an operational transformation initiative will compound their advantage.
